### WHY HEXNET IS HELD (do not deploy on the old Chris PASS)
Chris PASSed 916a37ebc. Nancy then returned PAUSE with 4 findings. #1 was stale (she read
the pre-fix file). The other THREE reproduced and Chris had not tested any of them:

1. **TRAINCHECK was memorisable.** Challenge 4 calls `random.seed(s)` in fixed order, so the
   module RNG sat at a known state and TRAINCHECK's draws were byte-identical across
   processes (verified DETERMINISTIC=True) -- while the page told students "randomised every
   run, so memorised weights cannot pass". FIXED: draws from `_tc_rng = random.Random()`
   (OS entropy). Re-verified 3 runs -> 3 different draws.
2. **Challenge 4's claim was cherry-picked -- 3rd unmeasured claim on this one challenge.**
   "zeroed 8/8, leaked <8" holds only on seeds 0-7: fails 12/25 windows, and WIDENING makes
   it worse (24/25 at N=32) since it demands perfection from a ~92% process.
   Measured over 120 seeds: zeroing 110/120 converged, median 0.0082, diverged 0/120;
   leaking 65/120, median 0.0000 (LOWER!), diverged 16/120.
   -> Leaking is NOT slower, it is UNSTABLE. Better lesson, and it is the real reason
   zero_grad exists. Rule is now the comparison `zeroed > leaked` over 16 seeds: 0/20
   window failures. Perfect-score test DELETED, not loosened.
3. **Challenge 1's randomness gate was a source regex** -- failed honest `random.gauss`,
   passed hardcoded weights carrying a dead `random.uniform` call (Nancy built the exploit).
   FIXED: functional two-neuron comparison (`distinct:` / `within_varies:`).

qc-hexnet.sh now gates the SHIPPED rule and hard-fails the build if it breaks.
QC green: cheat A rejected, false-fail 0/60, zeroed=16/16 leaked=13/16, rule HOLDS.

### GATE 5 (HexTalk) -- MEASURED FACTS, do not re-derive
Corpus = 3 sentences, vocab 27.
- Uniform perplexity = 27.00, EXACTLY the vocab size. Strong teaching fact.
- Bigram (add-1 smoothing) perplexity = 10.75 -> measured 2.51x better than uniform.

TEMPERATURE -- first metric was WRONG, second works:
- distinct-character count shows NO effect (26.8 vs 27.0 across temps 0.3-1.5). The
  metric SATURATES over a few hundred samples. Do not use it, and do not claim
  "low temp = more repetitive" on that basis.
- real-bigram share (fraction of sampled pairs that occur in the corpus) works, large
  and monotonic:  temp 0.2 -> 97.9% | 0.5 -> 49.4% | 1.0 -> 23.1% | 2.0 -> 15.6% | 5.0 -> 13.2%
- top-char share also works: 22.9% -> 12.7% -> 7.1% -> 5.9% -> 5.9%
- entropy works but saturates above temp 1.0 (3.24 -> 3.25), weaker signal.
THE CLAIM TO TEACH: low temperature makes the model play SAFE, reusing pairs it actually
saw; high temperature makes it INVENT pairs it never saw. Measured, not assumed.
Probes: scratchpad/hexnet/{bigram_probe,temp_probe}.py

BUILD RULE FOR GATE 5, learned the hard way in Gate 3: measure against the EXACT code
that ships, never a convenient harness. Three bad claims came from measuring a different
function. Wire every rendered number into qc-hextalk.sh the way qc-hexnet.sh now does.
